title: Internal Audit in Regulated Firms
summary: An eight-module programme giving internal auditors the tools to deliver risk-based assurance over the regulatory risks that matter most to boards and supervisors.
intro: This training programme equips internal auditors in regulated firms to plan and deliver risk-based assurance over compliance, conduct, financial crime, models and resilience, and to report findings that the audit committee and supervisors can rely on.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give internal auditors a practical grounding in auditing the risks that matter most to supervisors, from regulatory compliance and conduct to financial crime, AI and operational resilience. Participants leave able to plan risk-based coverage, test controls and outcomes rigorously, and report in a way that drives remediation and stands up to supervisory scrutiny.
sections.What It Covers: The role and independence of internal audit, risk-based audit planning, auditing regulatory compliance, conduct and culture, financial crime controls, models and AI, operational resilience and third parties, reporting to the audit committee, follow-up and working with supervisors.
Intended Audience: Heads of internal audit, audit managers and auditors in banks, insurers, investment firms, fund managers and payment firms
Co-sourced and outsourced audit providers delivering assurance to regulated firms
Audit committee members and compliance and risk staff who rely on internal audit work
Learning Objectives: Explain the role, independence and standards of internal audit in a regulated firm
Design a risk-based audit plan aligned with the firm's regulatory exposure
Apply audit techniques to compliance, conduct, culture and financial crime controls
Assess models, AI, operational resilience and third-party arrangements
Report findings to the audit committee and track remediation to closure
Engage constructively with supervisors and see the firm the way a supervisor does
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, audit planning exercises and report-writing practice, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's sector and audit plan.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of internal audit, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist technical background is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Internal Audit Function in Banks (2012)
Institute of Internal Auditors, Global Internal Audit Standards (2024)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)

modules.title: The Role and Independence of Internal Audit
modules.summary: What internal audit is for in a regulated firm, how it sits within the three lines of defence, and the structural safeguards that keep it independent and credible with supervisors.
objectives: Explain the purpose of internal audit and its place in the three lines of defence
Assess the independence, reporting lines and resourcing of the function
Identify what supervisors expect of internal audit and why it matters to them
syllabus: Internal audit's mandate, charter and unrestricted access
Independence, objectivity and the head of audit's reporting lines
Professional standards, quality assurance and external assessment
How supervisors use internal audit work and judge its quality

modules.title: Risk-Based Audit Planning
modules.summary: How to build an audit universe and a risk-based plan that reflects the firm's business model, regulatory exposure and emerging risks, and how to defend it to the audit committee.
objectives: Build an audit universe linked to the firm's risk profile and regulatory obligations
Prioritise audit coverage using risk assessment and supervisory priorities
Design a flexible plan that responds to change and emerging risks
syllabus: Audit universe, risk assessment and coverage cycles
Using risk registers, incidents, supervisory findings and horizon scanning
Balancing assurance, advisory and regulator-requested reviews
Agreeing and refreshing the plan with the audit committee

modules.title: Auditing Regulatory Compliance
modules.summary: How to audit the firm's compliance framework and its adherence to regulatory requirements, including the compliance function itself, regulatory reporting and the management of regulatory change.
objectives: Plan audits of the compliance framework and compliance monitoring
Test the accuracy and controls behind regulatory returns
Evaluate how the firm identifies and implements regulatory change
syllabus: Auditing the compliance function: mandate, resources and monitoring programme
Regulatory reporting: data lineage, reconciliations and sign-off
Regulatory change management and obligations registers
Breach identification, recording and notification to the authority

modules.title: Auditing Conduct, Culture and Customer Outcomes
modules.summary: How internal audit can give assurance on conduct, culture and the fair treatment of customers, moving beyond process testing to evidence of actual outcomes.
objectives: Design audit approaches to culture and behaviour
Test whether controls deliver fair customer outcomes in practice
Report soft-control findings credibly to management and the board
syllabus: Auditing culture: indicators, behavioural evidence and soft controls
Product governance, sales, complaints and vulnerable customers
Remuneration, incentives and conduct risk
Outcome testing and file review techniques

modules.title: Auditing Financial Crime Controls
modules.summary: How to audit the firm's anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, sanctions, fraud and anti-bribery controls, aligned with the risk-based approach set out in FATF standards.
objectives: Assess the firm's financial crime risk assessment and control framework
Test customer due diligence, monitoring and reporting effectiveness
Evaluate sanctions screening and fraud controls, including system tuning
syllabus: Business-wide risk assessment and the risk-based approach
Customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring and suspicious activity reporting
Sanctions screening: lists, thresholds, alerts and testing
Fraud, bribery and the governance of financial crime systems

modules.title: Auditing Models, Data and AI
modules.summary: How internal audit gives assurance over models, data and AI systems, including model risk management, data governance and the particular challenges of machine learning and generative AI.
objectives: Assess the firm's model risk management and AI governance framework
Audit data quality, model validation and ongoing monitoring
Use technology and analytics within the audit process itself
syllabus: Model inventory, tiering, validation and change control
Data governance, lineage and quality controls
AI-specific risks: explainability, bias, drift and third-party models
Data analytics and AI tools in audit work

modules.title: Auditing Operational Resilience and Third Parties
modules.summary: How to audit the firm's ability to withstand and recover from disruption, including important business services, cyber security, outsourcing and reliance on critical third parties.
objectives: Assess the mapping of important business services and impact tolerances
Audit cyber, incident management and scenario testing arrangements
Evaluate outsourcing and third-party risk management across the lifecycle
syllabus: Important business services, mapping and impact tolerances
Cyber security, incident response and business continuity, including ISO 22301
Outsourcing and third-party due diligence, contracts, oversight and exit
Concentration risk and reliance on intragroup and cloud providers

modules.title: Reporting, Follow-Up and Working with Supervisors
modules.summary: Brings the programme together: reporting findings to the audit committee, tracking remediation to closure, and building a constructive relationship with supervisors, ending with an audit improvement plan.
objectives: Write audit reports and committee papers that drive action
Run an effective issue-tracking and validation process
Engage confidently with supervisors and agree an improvement plan
syllabus: Report writing, ratings and the head of audit's annual opinion
Issue tracking, validation of remediation and escalation of overdue actions
Supervisory meetings, information requests and regulator-commissioned reviews
Workshop: an improvement plan for the internal audit function

related.title: Compliance Officer Academy
related.summary: A ten-module academy giving compliance officers the tools to run an independent, risk-based compliance function and handle supervisory engagement with confidence.

related.title: Internal Investigations and Interviewing Skills
related.summary: A nine-module programme giving control functions a structured method to investigate misconduct, whistleblowing reports and breaches, interview witnesses and subjects, and report findings.

related.title: Management and Leadership for Compliance and Risk Teams
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving managers of compliance, risk and financial crime teams the skills to lead the second line, influence the business and earn the board's confidence.

related.title: Professional Judgement and Core Skills for Compliance Staff
related.summary: A ten-module programme building the judgement, questioning, advisory and writing skills that compliance, risk and financial crime staff need to be trusted by the business, the board and the regulator.

related.title: Risk Management for Regulated Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving risk professionals the tools to design, run and evidence a risk management framework that informs decisions and withstands supervisory scrutiny.

related.title: Terrorist and Proliferation Financing Controls for Firms
related.summary: A nine-module programme equipping firms to assess, detect and report terrorist and proliferation financing, including screening, targeted financial sanctions and dual-use goods red flags.
